feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible. ELM single-column can simulate the snowpack (SWE, snowmelt flux) at each SNOTEL location and diagnose the day-of-year of snowmelt onset; the elevation control can be resolved by running one column per station and imposing the elevation difference through the DATM temperature/precip lapse-rate downscaling. However, ELM does not itself derive a lapse rate — it must be PRESCRIBED as forcing, and ELM single-column columns have no lateral coupling, so the 'local lapse rate on the same ridge' can only be tested by sensitivity experiments, not physically emergent.
answerable: Day-of-year of snowmelt onset at each SNOTEL location (from QFLX_SNOMELT / H2OSNO decline)
Simulated relationship between column base elevation and melt-onset DOY across stations
Sensitivity of melt-onset DOY to the imposed atmospheric temperature lapse rate for station pairs on the same ridge
Per-station SWE peak timing/magnitude and ablation rate
not_answerable: The true observed local atmospheric lapse rate (this is a forcing/observation input, not an ELM output)
Lateral/advective snow redistribution or slope-aspect radiation gradients between adjacent stations (single-column has no horizontal transport)
Sub-column terrain shading and wind-driven drift effects unless externally parameterized

parsed.n_justification: Six real Naches-basin SNOTEL sites are chosen to span the elevation gradient (~1370-1800 m) and to include two same-ridge pairs (Bumping Ridge/Morse Lake and White Pass/Pigtail Peak) so the local lapse rate can be resolved between neighboring stations rather than only across the whole basin.
requires_capabilities: DATM topographic/elevation lapse-rate downscaling (prescribed temperature + precip-phase adjustment per column base elevation)
ELM multi-layer snow physics (SNICAR albedo, refreezing, compaction)
Per-column site elevation and surface dataset overrides
High-frequency (daily) history output to detect melt-onset DOY
Multi-year spin-up to equilibrate soil temperature/moisture before analysis
assumptions: Atmospheric lapse rate is prescribed (baseline 6.5 K/km with sensitivity runs at 4.5 and 8.0 K/km) since ELM cannot derive it internally
Snowmelt onset DOY is defined as the first sustained day (3+ consecutive days) of positive QFLX_SNOMELT after peak H2OSNO
GSWP3/CLMGSWP3-style meteorological forcing is downscaled to each station elevation; observed SNOTEL SWE used only for validation, not as forcing
Same-ridge pairs (Bumping Ridge/Morse Lake; White Pass/Pigtail Peak) share aspect, so differences are attributed primarily to elevation via the imposed lapse rate
First 5 simulation years treated as spin-up and excluded from melt-onset climatology
No lateral snow redistribution or wind loading between columns
